messages:
maria (PM): Quick sync — hardware-aware onboarding prioritization. TL;DR: we need a scoring to decide which incoming models get fast-track onboarding based on hardware footprint, customer demand, and benchmark delta. Need buy-in on launch criteria and pinning rules by EOD.

aj (Eng): +1. Proposed scoring: customer_request_weight=0.4, perf_delta=0.3, hw_footprint=0.2, infra_risk=0.1. hw_footprint lowers score if model requires H100 vs L4. Simple to compute.

sam (ML): perf_delta needs per-hardware bench —can't compare A100 vs L4 token_latency raw. Suggest normalized speedup vs baseline (our gpt-small on same hw).

natalie (Solutions): Sales flagged several enterprise deals that explicitly need H100-only models. If customer is Dedicated and paying, they want a guaranteed fast-track. How does that change scoring?

maria (PM): Good q. Idea: if customer is on Dedicated and budgeted, add +0.25 to score; but the model must pass perf AND quality bench. We don't fast-track models with clear quality regressions.

aj (Eng): Implementation notes: in the catalog we tag model entries with `preferred_hardware` and `min_gpu_family`. Can wire to onboarding UI. Example config snippet: ```preferred_hardware: H100\nmin_gpu_family: h100\nbench_targets: {latency_p50: 80ms}```

sam (ML): Bench plan: run p95 latency, throughput under typical batch mix, and a prompt-suite of 200 prompts for quality. For quality acceptance use our eval harness: require quality drop <= 2% (measured by pass rate on labeled checks) and latency <= 1.5x baseline. If one variant (FP16 vs 4-bit) passes, flag both.

natalie (Solutions): Timeline ask from Customer X: needs cutover in 6 weeks. Can we promise that and what are the launch gates?

maria (PM): Launch gates draft: 1) perf pass per hardware family (p95 & p50), 2) quality regression <= 2% on our eval suite, 3) infra capacity reservation if Dedicated requested, 4) rollout plan with canary at 5% traffic and auto-fallback, 5) comms doc + customer opt-in + pricing delta signoff. For SLA customers add extended canary + runbook.

aj (Eng): Capacity reservation thought: Dedicated customers can reserve a "hardware bucket" but it's finite. Need to pick reservation strategy: static reservation (reserved GPUs) vs burst credits (guaranteed baseline + burst). Both have infra and billing implications.

sam (ML): Also callout quantization: 4-bit builds can change perf/quality. We should benchmark FP16 and 4-bit variants and gate them separately.

maria (PM): Decision needed: Pinning policy. Proposal: pin by model+hardware pair (e.g., `model-x@h100:1.0`) so fallback logic doesn't route incompatible variants to wrong hardware. Keep routing rules explicit. Thoughts?

aj (Eng): Agree. Also implement a compatibility shim that maps `model@h100` -> `model@h100-quant` or `model@a100` only when compatibility checks pass. Fallback rules: only route to lower hardware if quality preserved and an explicit override is set.

natalie (Solutions): From support POV, we need clear migration windows, pricing delta examples, and a template customer comms explaining why some models are hardware-restricted. Otherwise lots of confusion.

deploy-bot: Reminder: canary deploy window reserved for this model group at 3920202055 — will kick off if gates are green.

maria (PM): Next steps: aj to draft scoring formula + slide deck, sam to prototype the benchmark harness for H100/L4 within 5 working days, natalie to mock comms + pricing delta examples. Quick thumbs? :thumbsup: token: :sparkles:

aj (Eng): 👍 will post PR for scoring formula and an example computation.

sam (ML): 👍 starting harness + will include FP16/4-bit runs.

natalie (Solutions): 👍 I'll draft comms and pricing examples; will share with legal for wording.

maria (PM): Great — we'll reconvene after PRs land. If anyone wants to escalate a customer ask please ping me directly.
